scope: Selected claims only; does not establish deployed behavior or current law

claims.finding: Search routes choose body or metadata, construct filters, handle unavailable stores, and render legal_search.html.
Route loads document by id and renders legal_document.html via workspace page wrapper; missing documents and backend errors have separate handling.
Template provides session panel, prompt, optional scoped document and explicit limitation on legal currency; local stateless branch says history is unavailable.
Code redacts input/output, conditionally applies guardrails/cache, invokes RAG, logs and renders response. Persistence is online dependent; local stateless mode is not evidence of stored sessions.

Whole blocks are bounded by evidence count and approximate whitespace-token budget; optional expansion, filtering and rescue, no-context return, diagnostics and latency are present. Behavior depends on configuration and calls.
RetrievalOutcome and LegalRetriever with detailed retrieval methods are present; runtime retrieval not tested.
Expansion type and hash-checked document/candidate branch are present; runtime expansion not tested.

Interaction/session records include session_id, client_id, user_id; reads constrain by user_id or client_id when supplied. Development mode returns no persisted history. The data-layer functions alone do not guarantee every caller supplies an owner identifier.

limits: Current file hashes differ from historical evidence; no blanket re-binding, source snapshot, runtime or screenshot correspondence asserted. Remaining stale claims not reviewed.
